Pages/active_roof_leak_repair_charlotte_: Active roof leak repair · Charlotte, NC
Stop the water. Find the source. Repair the roof system.

The ceiling stain is often not directly below the roof opening. Majestic traces accessible evidence, controls active entry when safe and proposes the smallest reliable repair supported by the inspection.

Keep away from wet ceilings, light fixtures and electrical equipment. Place a container only if the area is safe, move valuables and call an electrician or emergency services when electricity or ceiling collapse is a concern.
Dripping during or after rain
Brown ceiling rings or bubbling paint
Wet insulation or musty attic odor
Leak near a wall, valley, vent or skylight
Recurring stain after an earlier patch
Protect people first and avoid wet electrical areas.
Move belongings and document the interior location.
Note when the leak starts: wind-driven rain, steady rain or after the storm.
Do not puncture or walk under a bulging ceiling.
Request a roof inspection as soon as conditions permit.

We record the stain or drip location and accessible attic evidence.

Pages/chimney_flashing_leak_repair_charl: Chimney and flashing leak repair · Charlotte, NC
A chimney leak needs more than another bead of caulk.

Water can enter through step flashing, counterflashing, the upslope cricket, roof-to-wall details, masonry or nearby shingles. Majestic documents the roof-side assembly and identifies when masonry work needs a separate specialist.

Keep water away from electrical fixtures and finished surfaces. Do not climb onto the roof or chimney. Active fire, smoke, gas or carbon-monoxide concerns belong with emergency authorities and qualified chimney professionals first.
Stain beside the chimney after rain
Loose, rusted or lifted metal flashing
Cracked sealant at counterflashing
Debris or standing water behind the chimney
Damaged shingles or underlayment at sidewalls
Record which side of the chimney shows moisture.
Note wind direction and rain intensity when it appears.
Protect the interior without entering unsafe areas.
Avoid applying random roof cement that can hide the actual path.
Schedule roof-side and accessible attic inspection.

Hail evidence must be inspected—not guessed from the ground.
Hail can affect shingles, ridge caps, vents, gutters and soft metals. Majestic records observable conditions and separates storm patterns from age, wear and unrelated installation conditions.

Pages/open_roof_hole_decking_repair_char: Open roof hole and decking repair · Charlotte, NC
An open roof needs a safe temporary plan and a layered rebuild.

An exposed opening may involve shingles, underlayment, plywood or OSB decking, framing and interior moisture. Majestic first controls access and water, then opens only what is needed to verify the permanent scope.

Keep everyone out from below an open or sagging area. Do not place weight on exposed decking. Electrical, structural, fire or collapse concerns require the appropriate emergency or licensed specialist first.
Visible daylight or open roof covering
Exposed, split or soft decking
Sagging between rafters or trusses
Water entering around a puncture
Debris, animal or branch penetration
Restrict access below the opening.
Protect belongings only from a safe location.
Photograph the opening from the ground or interior without touching it.
Call for emergency assessment before more rain.
Do not authorize a surface patch without understanding the substrate.
Safe stabilization
We determine whether temporary coverage can be installed safely or whether another trade must stabilize the area.
Controlled opening
Loose roofing is removed only as authorized to expose the full boundary of damaged material.
Deck and framing review
Affected plywood/OSB and visible framing are documented before replacement.
Layered rebuild
Approved decking, underlayment, flashing and roof covering are installed in the correct sequence.
Closeout

A roofing contractor documents the work. Your insurance carrier decides coverage.

Majestic Roofing inspects accessible roof areas, records visible conditions, prepares construction measurements and estimates, and explains its written roofing scope. With the homeowner’s authorization, the team may attend a scheduled adjuster visit and provide contractor scope clarification. Majestic Roofing is not a public adjuster, does not interpret policy language, does not negotiate coverage, and does not guarantee approval or payment.
NC Department of Insurance claims resource ↗
From storm concern to completed roof.
Each step has a defined owner, record and decision point. The homeowner and carrier manage the insurance claim; Majestic manages the roofing evidence and construction scope.

If a tree, open hole or active leak creates an immediate hazard, the first call may need to be 911, the utility, fire department or a qualified tree/structural professional. Majestic then confirms whether roof access is safe. When weather and conditions permit, temporary tarping may help limit additional water entry; the homeowner should preserve time-stamped photos, invoices and receipts.
Inspect the roof as a complete system

At the appointment, the technician first asks what happened, when it was noticed and which rooms are affected. The inspection can connect safe interior or attic evidence with the exterior roof area, then review accessible slopes, shingles, ridge and hip caps, valleys, flashing, pipe boots, vents, skylights, gutters, fascia, soffit and visible decking. Unsafe or inaccessible areas are clearly noted.

Majestic organizes wide-location photos, detail photos, notes, estimated measurements, roof geometry, affected components, material observations and the proposed repair or replacement scope. Visible storm patterns are separated from age, maintenance, installation details and hidden conditions. The record explains physical roofing work without interpreting the insurance policy.
Prepare for and coordinate the adjuster visit

The homeowner reports the event, opens the claim and schedules the carrier’s adjuster. With homeowner authorization and a confirmed appointment, Eric or another Majestic representative may attend the property to identify the same documented roof locations, answer technical construction questions and explain the contractor estimate. The carrier independently evaluates cause, coverage and payment.
Resolve construction scope, build and close out

Majestic compares its roofing scope with the available carrier estimate. If documented quantities or necessary construction components differ, the company may submit a factual contractor supplement with measurements, photos and supporting construction details. After the homeowner approves the written agreement, Majestic schedules materials and installation, completes cleanup and provides final photos, invoice, applicable warranty and requested completion documents.
What the free inspection appointment includes.
The goal is a clear, repeatable inspection—not a rushed photo from one roof spot. Safe access and property conditions determine which observations can be completed.
We record the event, discovery time, weather conditions, active leaks, prior repairs and the rooms or exterior sides involved.
The technician identifies electrical, tree, structural, surface, slope and weather risks before choosing ground, ladder, roof, attic or drone viewpoints.
Overview photos establish each slope and roof feature. Detail images then document the exact location and visible condition without relying on isolated marks.
Shingles, caps, valleys, flashing, penetrations, ventilation, decking indicators and attached drainage components are reviewed as one system.
Majestic explains what was observed, what remains unknown, whether temporary work is recommended and the next repair, replacement or documentation step.
The homeowner receives available photos, report, estimated measurements and the written roofing path so the next decision is based on the same factual record.
What storm damage can look like.

These are educational inspection examples—not photographs of a specific Majestic customer and not promises that a policy covers the condition. Select any image for safety steps, a detailed arrival process and repair options.
Displaced granules, circular marks or fractures in shingle mats, damaged ridge or hip caps, plus dents in gutters, vents, pipe boots or other soft metals.
Missing, lifted, creased or displaced shingles; affected ridge caps, separated flashing and damage at soffit, fascia or roof edges.
Branch penetrations, broken or exposed decking, crushed shingles, damaged gutters and openings that may require safe temporary protection.
Ceiling stains, attic moisture, wet decking and water paths that may begin upslope from the visible interior stain.
Lifted metal, failed transitions, open counterflashing, deteriorated sealant or nearby shingle damage can allow water beside a chimney.
Exposed, broken, soft or deteriorated plywood/OSB can require temporary protection, controlled removal and reconstruction by layers.
